story: Ray Boucher learned the business starting at his grandfather's Nashua store while still in high school. With his parents George and Lucille he opened Britches in 1983 in Eagle Square on Main Street in Concord. The shop began with men's measure-to-wear suits, custom dress shirts and upscale formal and casual wear, and later added women's measure-to-wear suits, professional attire and casual clothes. The shop calls itself a third-generation men's and women's clothier and haberdashery, and was featured on WMUR's NH Chronicle on 26 July 2023.

A full tailor shop is on the premises, fitting sizes from 38 Regular to 56XL. The shop also rents tuxedos. Its Menswear page names seven lines: 34 Heritage, Bench Craft, Ballin Slacks, Grand River, Enro, Robert Graham and Wigens Caps.

story: O'Connell's was established in 1959 and is a family-owned and -operated traditional clothier in Buffalo. The site's About page is signed by Bernhard John Huber, John Huber and Ethan A. Huber. It offers men's, women's and young men's clothing made in the USA, Canada and the UK, including three-button natural-shouldered sport coats and suits. The shop offers free alterations and custom suits, sport coats, topcoats and dress shirts, and is an agent for Barbour jacket restoration. Its Brands page lists 34 lines, including Alden, Barbour, Allen Edmonds, Quoddy and Schott NYC.
